\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{पद्मम्} (padmam)}{पद्मम् (padmam)}]{\sk{पद्मम्} (padmam) — a lotus}

\label{lesson:SA-C112-padmam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a leaf, then the Sanskrit for a flower.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{पद्मम्}}
\textbf{\sk{पद्मम्}} — \emph{padmam} — \textquotedblleft{}a lotus\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
MW links \emph{padma} \textquotedblleft{}a lotus\textquotedblright{} to \emph{pad} with a query mark, so its origin is uncertain. It lives on in Kashmiri \emph{pam-pōś} \textquotedblleft{}lotus\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7769).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{padmam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{padmam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{padmam}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a leaf, then the Sanskrit for a flower, then say \emph{padmam} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{नक्षत्रम्} (nakṣatram)}{नक्षत्रम् (nakṣatram)}]{\sk{नक्षत्रम्} (nakṣatram) — a star}

\label{lesson:SA-C112-naksatram}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a flower, then the Sanskrit for a lotus.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{नक्षत्रम्}}
\textbf{\sk{नक्षत्रम्}} — \emph{nakṣatram} — \textquotedblleft{}a star\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nakṣatra} \textquotedblleft{}a star\textquotedblright{}, and later a lunar mansion, is old, in the Rigveda; MW thinks it probably comes from the root √nakṣ \textquotedblleft{}approach, reach\textquotedblright{}. It lives on as Hindi \emph{nakhat} \textquotedblleft{}star, constellation\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6913).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{सूर्यः} (sūryaḥ)}{सूर्यः (sūryaḥ)}]{\sk{सूर्यः} (sūryaḥ) — the sun}

\label{lesson:SA-C112-suryah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a lotus, then the Sanskrit for a star.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{सूर्यः}}
\textbf{\sk{सूर्यः}} — \emph{sūryaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}the sun\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sūrya} \textquotedblleft{}the sun\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Indo-European (EtymDB): MW sets its base \emph{svar} \textquotedblleft{}sun, light\textquotedblright{} beside Latin \emph{sol} and Greek \emph{hēlios}, the source of English \emph{solar} and \emph{helium}. Hindi \emph{sūraj} \textquotedblleft{}sun\textquotedblright{} comes from it (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{भल्लूकः} (bhallūkaḥ)}{भल्लूकः (bhallūkaḥ)}]{\sk{भल्लूकः} (bhallūkaḥ) — a bear}

\label{lesson:SA-C112-bhallukah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a star, then the Sanskrit for the sun.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{भल्लूकः}}
\textbf{\sk{भल्लूकः}} — \emph{bhallūkaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a bear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bhallūka} \textquotedblleft{}a bear\textquotedblright{} has a disputed origin: CDIAL 9415 reports EWA's view that it may be Indo-European with an expressive \emph{-ll-}, and Przyluski's that it is Austroasiatic. It lives on as Hindi \emph{bhālū} \textquotedblleft{}bear\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9415).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{शृगालः} (śṛgālaḥ)}{शृगालः (śṛgālaḥ)}]{\sk{शृगालः} (śṛgālaḥ) — a jackal}

\label{lesson:SA-C112-srgalah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for the sun, then the Sanskrit for a bear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{शृगालः}}
\textbf{\sk{शृगालः}} — \emph{śṛgālaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a jackal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
MW calls \emph{śṛgāla} \textquotedblleft{}a jackal\textquotedblright{} (also written \emph{sṛgāla}) of doubtful derivation, so its origin is uncertain; it is old, in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. It lives on as Hindi \emph{siyār} and Bengali \emph{siyāl} \textquotedblleft{}jackal\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12578).
\end{cousinweb}
